title: See, Hear, Speak, Draw: Logan Kilpatrick & Simón Fishman
talk_summary: An OpenAI DevRel/apply-team talk demoing multimodal pipelines built by chaining separate models (GPT-4V for image description/comparison, DALL·E 3 for generation, Whisper for transcription) with text as the connective tissue. The only transferable engineering idea is the describe-compare-revise loop where a model critiques its own output against a target and regenerates.

takeaways.technique: Model-as-critic compare loop (target vs current, then revise)
takeaways.what_they_do: Generate an output, then feed both the target and the produced artifact back to a vision model asking it to enumerate differences, then regenerate from that diff list; iterate until close.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we give the two images to GPT with vision again um and we ask it to compare them and see what are some of the differences

takeaways.technique: Text as connective tissue between specialized models
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than one multimodal model, they chain narrow models by serializing intermediate results to text (image→description→prompt→image), keeping each hop a simple text interface.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can think of text as a connective tissue between all of these models

takeaways.technique: Sampled-frame + transcript summarization for long inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: For video they extract frames, caption each, transcribe audio, and merge into one long textual representation instead of feeding raw media.
